One Solve it system, and what to borrow from Count it and Build it (read-only) (2026-10-17)

What this is. An architecture and a migration plan for making every Solve it card one system, with each card only a problem type inside it. It is read from the code as it stands at main = 0415e23. No app code was changed, Count it and Build it were only read, and nothing was prototyped. The only new files are in docs/architecture/.

Read first: docs/scaffolds/SCAFFOLD-INVENTORY.md (shape ids S1-S7, D1-D2 and rung ids come from there), docs/lights-and-moves/LIGHTS-EXPERIMENT-REPORT.md, docs/design/SPEC-SOLVE-IT-LOOP.md rev 1.2, and the Add, Divide and Flip specs.

Lights round 2: not built. No branch or document for it exists (remote branches checked 2026-10-17; the newest lights work is round 1, merged into main behind ?ui=lights). Karl chose to run this report now anyway. Everything here about the manipulation layer is planned from round 1's code plus the prompt's description (reorder, combine by typing the sum, cross the border, distribute), and is marked inferred.

Observed = a file and line, a screenshot (shots/…, 1366×768, seed 7, dev server), or a script I ran. Inferred = my reading, with the reason.

Summary

  • Count it and Build it are already built the way Solve it needs. Every card is a pure reducer (newSession(problem) and reduce(state, action), no DOM) plus a separate drawing (renderMat(state) → <svg>), joined by a "play adapter" object with one shared shape (flipitPlay.js:14-45). Solve it's two cards already use the same adapter shape. So a Count it walk can run inside a Solve it rung unchanged, fed a sub-problem made from the current equation. Example: x = −3 + 5 → Combine it's problem −3 + 5.
  • What can be used unchanged: Combine it's light mode with its wrong-answer → support ladder (the missing x = b + k help), the big-number walk, Boxes & Circles' integer and like-term walks, Group It's group drawings, Groups of Terms' arrows, and Value it's filled-box substitution picture.
  • What needs an adapter: all of them, thinly. Each one must be given a sub-problem in its own data format and kept inside a reserved area of the Solve it screen. Their palettes, the bottom feedback line, the step bar, the streak and the 2.5 s auto-advance must be left behind. There are also size limits to work around (Flip It's counters stop at 12 per zone; Add's numbers go to 15).
  • The three biggest migration risks:
  • Moving Add onto the shared loop changes things students will notice (rungs restart per equation, Undo required after a red move, the choice at every state), and the lights experiment is wired to Add's private fields.
  • Student data and supports cross the section line. Solve it writes into Count it's device "skills" store and into the class sheet's supports column through lightStore.js. Embedding Combine it's help would start turning Count it's supports on for that device unless the adapter keeps its tags apart.
  • The look. There are eight separate counter drawings, and the colours mean different things in different areas (magenta is "opposite" in Count it but "negative" in Divide). Making it look like one system means either drawing new pieces or living with Count it's look, because Count it may not be edited.
  • Phase order I'd choose: P0 parity harness → P1 fix Add's two state-blind rungs in place → P2 shape classifier and lights → P3 scaffold registry and shared ladder, Divide first → P4 Add onto the loop with the lights wrapper carried across → P5 the new rungs (Undo first; count-and-cancel by embedding Combine it) → P6 pieces layer and one screen → P7 manipulation layer (after round 2 is tested) → P8 the other cards as configuration.
  • Questions: five, in Part 4, all answered by Karl on 2026-10-17.

Part 1. What Count it and Build it already have (read-only)

1B. Can Solve it use each one unchanged? The smallest adapter

All engines are pure and take plain data, so every one of them can be imported unchanged. The adapter is always a wrapper in Solve it's own code that does four jobs: - (1) Make the sub-problem from the current shape. - (2) Hold the sub-session as a field of the Solve it state, e.g. s.helper = { kind: 'combine', state }, and pass the helper's actions through. - (3) Draw its Mat inside the reserved scaffold area. The Mats are SVGs with a viewBox, so they scale. - (4) Leave the parts that belong to Count it's screen behind: palette, bottom feedback line, step bar, streak, auto-advance. Count it's light mode and walks make none of these themselves. main.js adds them around the adapter (main.js:155-163, 495-523), so a nested sub-session never triggers them. Observed: render() only reads the outer adapter.

Piece Use unchanged? Smallest adapter (Solve it side only) Limits to plan around

1D. What the three areas each draw their own way (a student would see the difference)

  • Eight counter drawings:
  • mat.js:36 (Flip It, Combine it)
  • lassoMat.js:52 (Group It; also Divide through groupDiagram)
  • boxMat.js:48 (Boxes & Circles)
  • termGroupMat.js:55 (Groups of Terms)
  • valueMat.js:56 (Value it)
  • addBothMat.js:69 (Add's seesaw)
  • solveMat.js:104 (the old one-step card)
  • groupDiagram.js:24's grid on top of counter

Their sizes and grouping differ: Add draws dashed group boxes on the seesaw (add-03); Count it draws loose counters in dashed zones (combineit-L1-c-stuck2). - Colours mean different things. - Magenta: --opposite is "always with an underline" and means "came from an opposite" (a rewritten term, a flipped group) in Count it and Build it (style.css:4, termPieces.js:7). Divide uses the same class for negative counters (groupDiagram.js:31, neg ? 'is-opposite' : 'is-inside'; div-02), so in Solve it magenta means "negative". - Green: --inside is "inside a group" (Group It); in Divide it means "positive". - Blue: --groups (#0072b2) is "how many groups" in Group It, and in Solve it the same blue means "the operation" and "click here". - Boxes and the opposite box. - Boxes & Circles draws −x as −□ (a box with a dash in front, boxes-L2-a-start). Karl's poster decision (branch claude/friendly-faraday-xzolrt, commit cdba0e4) is "opposite box −□". - SPEC-FLIP-IT.md §1 rev 1.0 said "never as 'a box with a minus'"; rev 1.1 (2026-10-17) now says −□, matching Boxes & Circles. - Divide draws x inside its boxes (div-02); Boxes & Circles draws an empty □ with a key "□ = x". They still differ (an x inside, or an empty □ with a key); not decided yet. - The screen. - Count it and Build it: the step bar on top, the feedback sentence at the bottom above the palette, a "?" button, a streak ("Streak 0 · Best 0"), a 2.5 s auto-advance. - Solve it: the line at the top, no step bar, no "?", no streak, nothing on a timer (loop §2). - The fonts differ too: Count it's problem and handwriting (Kalam) versus Solve it's stack. - A Count it piece embedded in Solve it must come without its frame, or the two styles will sit on one screen. - Signs. Count it writes −4 + 12 and 5 + (−8) (parentheses for a negative after +, combine.js:4-6). Add writes x + −6 and −6 + −3 (no parentheses, lightScreen.js:93-114). The same sum looks different in the two sections.

Part 2. One system: the target architecture

Layer 1. Engine: one state model, one loop

What solveLoop.js already provides (observed, solveLoop.js:1-285): - the choice at every state; - guesses and final values through the shared substitution renderer; - the forced-move rule; - commit (helpful → new state; unhelpful → needUndo), folding and foldNext; - Undo of only the unfolded move; - Start over; - the help ladder with rungs reset per state; - Teach me; - the answer-row rules; - card hooks: reduce, rungs, teach, answerBlocked, answerOpen, afterUndo, nextNeeded, movePromptKey, undoKey, params, touched.

What Add's reducer does that the loop cannot today (observed in addBothMoves.js): 1. A stage other than moves. The build stage at L2-L3 (:180-185), and the resolving interlude while Party/Battle pairs are combined (:402, 547-552). The loop knows only moves and done. Needed: a card-owned phase the loop checks before its own actions (it already lets card.reduce go first, solveLoop.js:152). 2. A two-action move inside the scaffold (pending half-moves and tilt, :365-390). This fits as card or rung state, but answerLive/helpOk need a hook for "a half-move is open" (answerBlocked exists). 3. Moves that aren't judged (Trade places, :344-356): it rewrites the board without lights and doesn't count as red. Needed: commit({ judged: false }). 4. No Undo gate, and the path is fixed per problem. These are older rules; the loop's are the spec's (inventory Q1). This is a behaviour change, not a missing feature. 5. Its own substitution (substitutionSteps, :604-620, sub.step >= 3 hard-coded). It goes away: the loop's renderer already passes Add's cases (audit registry #3).

Verdict (inferred from the hooks): the loop needs three small additions (a card phase, judged: false, a "help may open here" hook), not a rewrite. Add is the card that has to change.

Layer 2. Shape classifier

shapeOf(state) and lightsOf(prevShape, shape) as in the inventory 3B, in a new engine/solveit/shape.js. It must be order-free and sign-normalised, and take the state, not just the board, because waiting-for-Undo is a flag.

One board model for every card (inferred from what the coming cards need). A side is a list of terms: - {kind: 'x', coef} (coef may be a fraction later), - {kind: 'num', v}, - {kind: 'frac', n, inner} (Divide's ⅟a(b)), - {kind: 'group', n, inside: [terms]} (Distribute).

Add's and Divide's boards are already subsets of this (addBothMoves.js:20-27, divideMoves.js:15-19).

Converters to Count it / Build it formats: - toFlipIt(b, k) → {left, op, right} - toTerms(side) → [{kind: 'x'|'int', op, value}] - toTermGroups(group)

They live in Solve it's code (layer 3's helpers), so nothing in Count it or Build it changes.

Lights. Solved for x and One box read one shape; Fewer terms and Smaller numbers compare two shapes. This replaces: - Add's judge (addBothMoves.js:84-88), - Divide's hard-coded smaller: 'green' (divideMoves.js:227), - the classic panel's copying of Fewer terms' green into six other lights (lightScreen.js:288).

Layer 3. Scaffold registry

A rung is a small object:

{ id: 'S2.count', shows: 'counters', does: 'cancel pairs, count, type x', uses: ['combine'],
  when: (shape, slip) => shape.id === 'S2',
  open(state, shape) → state,          // reads shape.params, never state.problem
  reduce(state, action) → state | undefined,
  view: 'helper' | 'seesaw' | 'groups' | 'line-only' }
  • The registry is shape id → ordered rungs. A known slip picks only where to start (inventory Q5).
  • The ladder machinery stays in the loop: the stuck count, reset per state, the supports log with old names plus a shape field.
  • Helpers: rungs that embed a Count it or Build it engine hold it in s.helper and pass actions through.
  • Teach me is the same rungs in forced mode.

Which existing rungs move in (from inventory 3D): - as they are: A-REM, A-SEE, A-BUILD, A-TWO, A-ZERO, D-MODEL, D-DEAL, D-PIC, D-GUIDE, D-DIAG1, D-DIAG2; - after a rewrite to read the shape: A-GUIDE and A-TEACH; - new: - "Undo first" (every waiting state), - S2 count-and-cancel (embeds C1, C4 for sizes 13+), - S5 (embeds C5's integer mode), - DF "why it didn't split" (Divide's own boxes).

Layer 4. Cards as configuration

export default card({
  id, title, levels: [{ forms, ranges, mixes, live: ['add'], lights: ['fewer','solved'], collapse: false }, …],
  generate(level, seed),                 // verified by substitution (the shared generator checks)
  start(problem) → board,
  moves: { add: { amount: 'integer', apply(board, k) → { rows, next } } },   // or fraction, flip, trade, …
  slips: { typed: tag(p, v) → tag, messages }, words: { … },
  firstGuess: 'force-next' | 'owe-same',  // the loop rule, or the lights experiment's
})

Layer 5. Manipulation layer

Round 1's pattern is already right (observed): withLights(reduce) wraps a reducer (addBothLights.js:72) and keeps hover/preview/focus in s.ui, the same pattern as the tucked layout's withTuckedUi (tuckedLayout.js:30).

Target: one withManipulation(loop.reduce). - Gestures become loop actions: - drop a number into the blank → setAmount; - type the sum → combine (a new loop action: the student's own combining replaces S2 → S7, and is the only way S7 is reached); - drag a term across = → cross (Cross the border, a move); - reorder → a view-only change, or reorder with judged: false; - drag a number onto a group → distribute. - The engine keeps one canonical board; the shape classifier ignores order. Round 2's own details are unknown (not built), so this is inferred.

Layer 6. Pieces library

A view/solveit/pieces.js with one look: - counter(sign), box({ opposite }), group(…), bar(n, kept), seesaw(items). - Can it be a thin layer that re-exports Count it's drawings? Only partly (observed from the exports): - lassoMat.js exports el and counter; valueMat.js exports boxShape and modelLayout. Those can be re-exported unchanged. - Boxes & Circles' box and opposite-box drawing (boxMat.js pieceNode, counterMarks) and Flip It's counter (mat.js:36) are not exported. Solve it can only use them by embedding the whole Mat, or by drawing its own copy, which adds a ninth counter drawing. - Recommendation (inferred): - Solve it's pieces layer draws its own counter and boxes once, matching Count it's look (the same marks, sizes and colour tokens), and re-exports counter/boxShape where they fit. - Embedded Count it Mats keep their own drawing. This is the honest cost of "don't touch Count it": some inconsistency stays inside embedded helpers (Q2).

Layer 7. The screen

  • One component (view/solveit/screen.js) for every card: the line, the stack (one row builder), x = [ ], the panel (moves + Goals lights from lightsOf), the help corner, the pad, and a reserved tray for pictures and helpers.
  • Today there are four copies: lightScreen.js, solveScreen.js, lightsScreen.js, tuckedLayout.js (audit registry #2, #5, #6).
  • The tucked shell and round 1's lights layout are the two candidates; Karl's tests should pick one (Q1).

Part 3. Migration plan

Rules for every phase. It ships on its own, behind a flag where behaviour changes. Count it and Build it files are never edited. The class sheet keeps its old words (supports: hint, model, move, guided, crossoff, forced), and a new shape field is added, never renamed.

Parity tests, run on every phase: - (a) Problems: the same seeds give the same problems, for every card and level (snapshot generate(level, seed) for seeds 1-200). - (b) Save codes: the same save codes (encode/decode round trip of every level combination, v14). - (c) Class-sheet records: for scripted runs of each card, the same makeRecord output (eventlog.js:10-24) apart from the new shape field. - (d) Screens: screenshots equal with the flag off (the dev-server script used for these reports, at 1366×768). - (e) Count it and Build it: their own tests and screenshots unchanged (they must not move at all).

Add it to the loop, never to the card

Why this order, against the prompt's (a)-(g): - P0 comes first because every later phase claims parity, and nothing measures it today (the audit found no screen tests). - P1 is pulled forward: it's a two-line bug fix that students feel now, and waiting for P4 means months. - The registry starts on Divide (P3) before Add moves: Divide is already on the loop, so the registry is proven on the easy card. - The count-and-cancel rung (P5) waits until after the Add port (P4), so it's built once, in the registry, not first in Add's private climb.

Carrying the lights experiment across in P4 (so it isn't built twice). Observed: withLights(reduce = reduceAddBoth) already takes the reducer as a parameter (addBothLights.js:72), so it can wrap loop.reduce instead. What it reads from Add's private state has to be mapped:

Part 4. Questions (batch 1)

Recommended option first. Answers are recorded here when given.

Q1. Which screen becomes the one Solve it screen? - (A) Recommended: decide after your classroom test of lights round 1/2. Until then, build the layers (P0-P5) so they don't care which screen draws them. Evidence: two shells are being tested now, the tucked layout on Divide and the lights layout on Add, and they disagree on where the moves and help go. - (B) The tucked shell now. - (C) The lights layout now.

Answer (Karl, 2026-10-17): (A). Decided after the classroom tests.

Q2. When a Count it helper runs inside a Solve it rung, how much of Count it's look is acceptable? - (A) Recommended: its Mat and drawing as they are (its counters, its fonts), but never its frame (step bar, bottom line, streak, palette, auto-advance). Solve it's line and pad drive it. Evidence: the Mats are separable SVGs (renderMat returns one <svg>); the frame comes from main.js, not the Mat. - (B) Redraw it all in Solve it's own pieces. This duplicates the drawing and means the engines must expose more than they do. - (C) The whole Count it screen, as is, in a panel.

Answer (Karl, 2026-10-17): close to (A). Count it's pictures need not match exactly, but the feel must not be considerably different.

Q3. The opposite box: which drawing is the system's? - (A) Recommended: −□ (a box with a dash in front), as Boxes & Circles draws it and your poster decision says. Change SPEC-FLIP-IT.md §1 to match. Evidence: boxes-L2-a-start; branch claude/friendly-faraday-xzolrt commit cdba0e4. - (B) A separate opposite-box drawing (Flip spec §1), which Count it wouldn't have. - (C) Decide when Flip it is built.

Answer (Karl, 2026-10-17): (A). −□, as Build it draws it. SPEC-FLIP-IT.md is now rev 1.1 to match.

Q4. Should help used inside Solve it count toward Count it's supports (the device "skills" that keep a support switched on)? - (A) Recommended: no. Solve it's helpers start with no skills, and their tags stay out of afterProblem. Evidence: lightStore.js:25-29 updates Count it's skills from every Solve it problem's tags; Combine it's tags would match SKILL (scaffold.js:69-75) and change Count it. - (B) Yes: one student, one set of supports across sections. - (C) Count them, but in a separate store.

Answer (Karl, 2026-10-17): (A). Help used in Solve it does not switch on Count it's supports; a shared record is a later decision.

Q5. Magenta and green: what do they mean in Solve it? - (A) Recommended: keep Count it's meanings (magenta = came from an opposite; green = inside a group). Divide's negative counters become black − marks like Count it's. Evidence: style.css:4-7; groupDiagram.js:31 uses is-opposite for "negative". - (B) Keep Divide's (magenta = negative) and accept that the sections differ. - (C) Decide in the palette pass (lights-and-moves Q8).

Answer (Karl, 2026-10-17): (C). Decided in the colour pass.
